subject: coxph doesn't work in joint likelihood model, exponential/weibull/lognormal does

messages.author: 93a768cdebfde0f1
messages.subject: coxph doesn't work in joint likelihood model, exponential/weibull/lognormal does
parts:
Greetings,
      
The following code is from Dr. Gomez-Rubio's bitbucket chapter on joint longitudinal/survival models: https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/inla-gitbook/ch-survival.html#model-with-no-shared-terms

library("JMbayes")
data(prothros)
#Number of observations in each dataset
n.l <- nrow(prothro)
n.s <- nrow(prothros)

#Vector of NA's
NAs.l <- rep(NA, n.l)
NAs.s <- rep(NA, n.s)
#Vector of zeros
zeros.l <- rep(0, n.l)
zeros.s <- rep(0, n.s)

#Long. and survival responses
Y.long <- c(prothro$pro, NAs.s)
Y.surv <- inla.surv(time = c(NAs.l, prothros$Time),
                    event = c(NAs.l, prothros$death))

Y.joint <- list(Y.long, Y.surv)

#Covariates
covariates <- data.frame(
  #Intercepts (as factor with 2 levels)
  inter = as.factor(c(rep("b.l", n.l), rep("b.s", n.s))),
  #Time
  time.l = c(prothro$time, NAs.s),
  time.s = c(NAs.l, prothros$Time),
  #Treatment (longitudinal)
  treat.l = c(as.integer(prothro$treat =="prednisone"), NAs.s),
  #Treat.s
  treat.s = c(NAs.l, as.integer(prothros$treat =="prednisone"))
)

#Indices for random effects
r.effects <- list(
  #Patiend id (long.)
  id.l = c(prothro$id, NAs.s),
  #Patient id (surv.)
  id.s = c(NAs.l, prothros$id)
)

joint.data  <- c(covariates, r.effects)
joint.data$Y <- Y.joint

pro.joint.inla <- inla(Y ~ -1 + inter +
                         # Longitudinal part
                         f(id.l) + 
                         time.l + treat.l +
                         #Survival part
                         treat.s,
                       data = joint.data, family = c("lognormal", "weibull.surv")
)

The code works similarly for other parametric survival models such as the exponential.surv and lognormal.surv likelihoods. However, when I try to use the semi-parametric coxph likelihood, the call fails to recognize that Y[[2]] is an inla.survival object:

sapply(joint.data$Y,class)
[1] "integer"   "inla.surv"
pro.joint.inla.COXPH <- inla(Y ~ -1 + inter +
                          # Longitudinal part
                          f(id.l) + 
                          time.l + treat.l +
                          #Survival part
                          treat.s,
                        data = joint.data, family = c("lognormal", "coxph")
)
Error in inla.coxph(formula, data, control.hazard, debug = debug) : 
  For survival models, then the reponse has to be of class `inla.surv'; you have `list'

Has anyone else encountered this issue? Or is there something fundamental I'm misunderstanding about why the coxph model can't be used here whereas the parametric models can?

Thanks for your time.
-tyler
